name: University of East Anglia

settingEvidence.evidence: see what it’s really like to study at a campus university

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK students starting in 2027/28. UEA says this is the UK government's announced fee cap for 2027-28 and that Home fees will change if the cap changes; fees also rise each year for students already studying.

source.evidence: the tuition fee cap for UK undergraduate students for the 2026-27 academic year would increase to £9,790 and the 2027-28 academic year would increase to £10,050

livingCosts.text: UEA halls cost about £131–£209.50 a week in 2026/27 on the usual 41-week undergraduate licence: rooms sharing a bathroom £131, en suite rooms £178.50–£209.50. En suite twin rooms shared with another student cost £97.50 each.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open days: Saturday 24 October 2026 and Saturday 28 November 2026. 2027 dates are not announced yet.

source.evidence: Our undergraduate Open Day dates are: ... Saturday 24 October 2026 ... Saturday 28 November 2026

contextual.summary: If you live in England and qualify under one of UEA's contextual schemes, you can get an automatic contextual offer with lower entry requirements (BBC instead of ABB on its economics courses).
contextual.typicalReduction: Not stated in general; on the seven courses recorded here the contextual A-level offer is BBC compared with a typical ABB.

criteria.detail: If you live in England, UEA uses your postcode to check whether you live in an area of deprivation, measured with the Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD). Which IMD areas qualify isn't shown in the page text; use UEA's postcode eligibility checker on its 2027-entry page.
'Outreach Activity Participants' is one of UEA's contextual admissions schemes. The page text doesn't say which outreach activities count.

contextual.rulesText: You don't need to apply: UEA's admissions team works out your contextual offer automatically from data it and its partners already hold, if you live in England. UEA's schemes for 2027 entry are Nationwide Contextual Admissions, Outreach Activity Participants, Preparing for Medicine participants, Preparing for Pharmacy participants, Access to HE students and Medicine with a Gateway Year. All GCSE and subject requirements stay the same for contextual offers. The 2027-entry page has a postcode eligibility checker (https://www.uea.ac.uk/apply/undergraduate/contextual-admissions/2027-entry); the detailed rules for each scheme aren't shown in the page text.

source.evidence: If you are living in England and applying for an undergraduate course you may be eligible for contextual admissions through one of our schemes ... All GCSE and subject requirements will remain for all contextual offers

notes: No 2028-entry course pages yet (checked 2026-10-21: the 2028-29 address of the BSc Economics course page returns 'Not Found'), so all courses use 2027 entry (September 2027 start).
UEA is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and none of the course pages names an admissions test.

All seven courses ask for ABB at A level (contextual offer BBC) and list no required A-level subjects. The economics subject page says you can study economics without A-level maths or economics and that students with any subjects are welcome (https://www.uea.ac.uk/study/subjects/economics).
Every recorded course also has Year Abroad and Placement Year versions listed as course options.
UEA estimates living expenses at £1,171 a month (2027/28 course pages: https://www.uea.ac.uk/course/undergraduate/bsc-economics/2027-28).

Halls rents are for 2026/27 on a 41-week undergraduate licence (https://assets.uea.ac.uk/f/185167/x/85f91e4351/residence-type-room-comparison.pdf). UEA says halls licences mean you do not pay bills such as internet, gas and electricity (https://www.uea.ac.uk/uea-life/accommodation).

Not added, to keep to seven courses: BSc Accounting and Finance (N400), BSc Business Finance and Economics and BSc Finance and Management (all Norwich Business School) and the final-year-entry courses.
UEA's neaco / Take Your Place outreach is for students in areas of East Anglia, so it isn't recorded as a programme.
